ai.description: *Ghatixalus variabilis* is a 4–6 cm frog with a bright green dorsum, dark brown flanks, and yellow-spotted limbs. It is distinguished by its translucent belly and prominent, golden-rimmed eyes.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ghatixalus variabilis* is best distinguished by the presence of distinct, dark-edged, bright yellow or orange spots on its flanks and the hidden surfaces of its thighs.
ai.habitat: *Ghatixalus variabilis* inhabits evergreen forests and high-altitude shola grasslands in the Western Ghats, typically found near streams at elevations above 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: *Ghatixalus variabilis* is primarily nocturnal, remaining camouflaged against mossy rocks during the day and emerging at night to forage for small insects near forest streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ghatixalus variabilis* is an oviparous breeder that deposits eggs in gelatinous clutches on vegetation overhanging water. Breeding occurs during the monsoon (June–August).
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ghatixalus variabilis* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in high-elevation evergreen forests (above 1,000 m) across Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
ai.callDescription: The call of *Ghatixalus variabilis* consists of a series of short, high-pitched metallic "peeps" emitted by males perched on vegetation near fast-flowing mountain streams.
